plan: This auction functions like a second-price auction: my sealed bid sets my exit point in the ascending clock, and I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the winner pays the highest losing bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so (when my value exceeds others' bids) and never pay more than my value if I win. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid $18, my true value.

This is effectively a second-price auction structure - my sealed bid acts as my maximum exit price, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (or the clock price when others exit), not necessarily my own bid. Bidding my true value ($21) is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is below my value but above my lower bid.
